newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia tax police confirm block Baltic accounts.
newsitem.headline: Russia tax police confirm block Baltic accounts.

text.p: The St Petersburg tax police confirmed on Thursday that it had suspended operations on the correspondent accounts of Baltic banks in the city following what it called serious breaches of banking laws.
Baltic media had reported the blocking of the accounts but there had been confusion over which banks had been hit.
"The operations on these correspondent accounts have been suspended," spokesman Vladimir Alexandrov told Reuters.
He said that money was allowed to enter the accounts but could not be withdrawn.

Alexandrov said the suspension would be in force until the banks paid 200 billion roubles ($34.4 million), which the police estimated was the loss to the Russian budget in the first half of 1997 as a result of the operations.
He said Baltic banks opened correspondent accounts with Russian banks through which Russian companies transferred funds to Russian companies in the Baltic states.
No taxes, including value added tax, were paid on the transactions which represented deals between the companies.
He said the banks involved were Latvia's Multibanka, Saules Bank, Banka Victoriya, Aikraukles Bank, the Latvian Economy Bank, Kapital Banka and Pareks Bank.
In Estonia, he said that Forekspank, Tallinna Pank, Maapank and Krediidipank had been suspended.
In Lithuania, he named only Snoras Bank although local media said that the account of Siauliu Bank had also been hit.
The Latvian central bank and banking association have sent strong protests over the freezing of the accounts while several of the banks have said they would fight the order in the courts.
